svg.text: PART 10: PUSH BUTTON AND STATUS LED
Test setup for step 3. Only the laptop USB is needed: the button uses the STM32 internal pull up, the LED is driven by a pin.
USB cable to the laptop (power and code)
LED: long leg (+) in row a,
short leg (flat side) in the rail
on the feeder body, 2 wires soldered to it
Not bought yet: touch the two wire ends together to test
Column map of the whole feeder:
Button: Nucleo D8 · PF12 to column 49
LED: Nucleo D1 · PG14 to column 44
the other to the bottom − rail (column 52)
No 3.3 V wire needed in this circuit
PF12: input, internal pull up, interrupt
on the falling edge: free 3.3 V, pressed 0 V
100 nF + pull up smooth the bounce (a few ms)
Kibbly hardware · circuit 10 of the circuits by part · wires B1 to B4 and L1 to L3 in hardware/04_wiring_list.md section 12, rail R3 in section 4B
